preamble: In several Indo-Aryan languages the retroflex nasal /ɳ/ is realized as a nasalized retroflex flap [ɽ̃] outside clusters with retroflex stops. The same thing happens to /ɖ/, which is flapped to [ɽ] after vowels. Instead of a full stop closure, the tongue tip makes a single ballistic flap while the velum stays lowered. The flapped allophone is documented with word forms for Hindi. In Gujarati, word-final /ɳ/ varies freely between [ɳ] and [ɽ̃] (Mistry 1997).

examples.note: /ɳ/ does not occur word-initially; outside clusters it has the nasalized flap [ɽ̃] as a common allophone

context: Outside clusters with retroflex stops: after vowels and word-finally in Hindi and Marathi
